title: Research
text: Our lab studies infectious disease transmission at the interfaces among people, animals, and the environment. We use environmental surveillance and quantitative epidemiologic approaches to understand where pathogens are circulating, how they move, and how environmental data can support public health decision-making.

title: Research
text:
Environmental pathogen surveillance
We develop and apply methods for detecting infectious disease threats in environmental samples, including wastewater, air, water, and other complex matrices.
Our work spans assay development, sample processing, interpretation of environmental signals, and integration with clinical and epidemiologic surveillance.
Example questions

What can environmental surveillance reveal before or beyond clinical testing?
How do pathogen concentrations vary across environmental matrices?
How should environmental measurements be interpreted in relation to cases, prevalence, or transmission?

title: Research
text:
One Health and cross-species transmission
Many emerging infections move across human, animal, and environmental systems. We study these interfaces directly, with particular interest in zoonotic pathogens and settings where occupational, agricultural, and environmental exposures overlap.
Example questions

What environmental pathways may contribute to pathogen spread between species?
Where can environmental sampling complement animal or human surveillance?
How can surveillance systems better capture risks at human–animal interfaces?

title: Research
text:
Infectious disease transmission and exposure
Detection alone is not enough. We pair environmental measurements with epidemiologic data to investigate transmission processes and exposure pathways.
Example questions

Which environmental pathways plausibly contribute to infection risk?
How do pathogen persistence and partitioning affect exposure?
How can environmental data improve transmission models?

title: Research
text:
Genomic and quantitative methods
We use molecular, genomic, statistical, and computational approaches to make environmental pathogen data more informative.
Methods may include targeted molecular assays, metagenomic sequencing, phylogenetics, spatial analysis, exposure modeling, and infectious disease modeling.

title: People
text: We are building an interdisciplinary team at the intersection of environmental health, infectious disease epidemiology, microbiology, and quantitative methods.

title: Paulos Lab
section: Linking environmental evidence to infectious disease transmission
text:
Linking environmental evidence to infectious disease transmission
Our work combines environmental microbiology, epidemiology, molecular methods, genomics, and quantitative modeling to understand pathogen circulation across human, animal, and environmental systems.

title: Paulos Lab
section: From environmental detection to transmission insight
text:
From environmental detection to transmission insight
Environmental surveillance can reveal pathogen circulation that traditional clinical surveillance may miss. Our work asks not only whether pathogens can be detected in the environment, but what those measurements tell us about transmission, exposure, and public health action.
Read about our research →

title: Join the Lab
text: We are interested in working with students and researchers who want to understand infectious disease transmission using environmental, epidemiologic, and molecular data.

title: Join the Lab
section: Who might be a good fit?
text:
Who might be a good fit?
You do not need to arrive with experience in every method we use. Strong candidates may come from epidemiology, environmental health, microbiology, engineering, data science, public health, or related fields.
Interests that fit especially well include:

environmental surveillance
infectious disease epidemiology
One Health and zoonotic disease
environmental microbiology
molecular methods and sequencing
spatial or infectious disease modeling
quantitative exposure assessment

title: Join the Lab
text:
Current opportunities

Undergraduate and master’s students
I work with undergraduate students at the University of Michigan through the UROP program, and with MS and MPH students in the School of Public Health and beyond. If you’re interested in research for credit or for paid opportunities, email me to discuss.


Prospective doctoral students
Apply to the Doctoral Program in Epidemiologic Science at the University of Michigan School of Public Health. More information is available on the Epidemiologic Science PhD program page.


Research staff and postdoctoral researchers
Links to open positions will be listed here when applicable. For prospective postdoctoral fellows, contact me to discuss possibilities.

title: Join the Lab
text:
Mentoring approach
We aim to build a collaborative research environment where people receive clear expectations, regular feedback, opportunities for intellectual ownership, and support in developing an independent scientific identity. People from all backgrounds are welcome in the Paulos Lab.

title: Join the Lab
text:
How to contact us
If you are interested in joining the lab, email paulos@umich.edu with:

a brief description of your research interests
why the lab’s work interests you
your CV or resumé
the type of position or training opportunity you are seeking
